title: Chanan the Tailor

paragraphs: In [Avodah Zarah 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.39a.14-15), Rav Huna bar Minyomi bought tekhelet from members of Rav Amram Chasida’s household and came before Rav Yosef, who did not have [an answer]. Chanan the tailor met him and said to him: “What does Yosef the poor know? A case happened to me: I bought tekhelet from members of the household of Ravnai, the brother of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, and I came before Rav Mattenah, who did not have [an answer]. I came before Rav Yehudah of Hagronia (in Rabbeinu Chananel and Dikdukei Soferim the word ‘of Hagronia’ is absent), who said to me, ‘You have fallen into my hand,’” etc. Hyman explains this as what Yuchasin meant in writing “chapter HaTekhelet”: it means that he is mentioned in connection with the law of tekhelet.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The Bavli calls him Rav Yehudah of Hagronia. In the linked [Rabbeinu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Avodah_Zarah.39a.13), Rav Yehudah has no place-name attached. A similar-looking word belongs to the following reply and is glossed there.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1414&lang=en) likewise locates the tekhelet episode in Avodah Zarah. Hyman understands Yuchasin’s chapter label as a reference to the subject and reports the omission of “of Hagronia” in Dikdukei Soferim.
